_what: Barcelona base, 26 Sep - 11 Oct 2026, 15 nights. Visiting family, so roughly half the days are family days and half are excursions. Researched to tools/STOP_SPEC.md, built to tools/NEW_TRIP.md. Dates are FIXED by flights and cannot move.

brief.base: Barcelona city (family). Rental car for the whole stay.
brief.radius: All of Catalonia - LLuis set this explicitly, overriding the 30-minute default in STOP_SPEC. Drive time is still recorded for every entry and the list is still sorted nearest-first, because it is what decides whether a day works, not whether it qualifies.
brief.split: About half family days, half excursions.
wants: small towns he has not seen
the best food on each excursion
constraint_notes: LLuis is from Barcelona. The famous set is assumed seen unless he says otherwise; he is cutting the candidate list himself rather than listing what he has done.
No motorhome, no towed truck, no dog and no cat on this trip. The Alaska rig rules, the 40 ft length rule and the bike-carrier gravel question do NOT apply and must not be inherited.
brief.return_rule: Most excursions must return to Barcelona the same day. One or two overnights out are allowed. LLuis set this explicitly - it is what demotes the far corners (Val d'Aran, Aiguestortes, Mont-rebei, Terra Alta, the Ebre delta) from day trips to the one-or-two overnight slots, or off the card entirely.
brief.who: LLuis plus his mother and family on the day trips. This is the single most important filter on this trip and it OVERRIDES the Alaska default of 'easy and moderate lead'. Every walk has to work for a mixed-age group: short, low gradient, firm underfoot, no exposure, no scrambling, and somewhere to sit and something to eat at the end. Where a longer or harder extension exists it is recorded as an OPTION for whoever wants it, never as the walk itself.
brief.family_days: Flexible - no fixed family commitments. The calendar can be built around the hard opening constraints (Saturday-only, Sunday-only, Monday closures) rather than round family dates.
brief.food_register: Best LOCAL cooking, not starred destination dining. What the town is actually good at, at a table a family can sit down at. Closing days matter more than accolades - a great restaurant shut on Monday is not a recommendation.
brief.merce_sitges_method: LLuis asked to use LAST YEAR as the reference for both, since neither 2026 programme is published yet: La Merce 2025 and the 58th Sitges Festival (2025). Model what to expect from those, and flag clearly that it is a pattern from last year, not a 2026 listing.
brief.walk_limit: About 4 km is comfortable for the group, mother included - LLuis's own figure. That is a real budget, not a ceiling to aim at: 4 km of flat, firm path is a different thing from 4 km of rough ground, so distance is chosen with the surface, not against it. It retires the earlier 'assume very short' assumption.

flights.note: Arrival day is a half day - on the ground 13:15, plus passport queue and the drive in. Departure day gives a morning only; BCN airport wants you there by about 12:30.

stop.name: Barcelona
stop.blurb: Fifteen nights based in Barcelona with family, and a rental car for the whole stay. Half the days belong to the family; the rest are day trips out into Catalonia, chosen for small towns and beaches LLuis has not already seen, walks that work for a mixed-age group, and the best local cooking rather than destination dining. The trip lands inside La Merce and ends inside the Sitges festival, neither of which was planned.

events.name: La Merce 2026 - Barcelona's Festa Major
events.impact: Lands on arrival. He is on the ground 26, 27 and 28 Sep, which is the closing weekend - the part with the piromusical, correfoc, castellers and the giants. No travel needed: it is happening where he is staying.
needs: The per-district breakdown was still pending on the programme site
events.CORRECTION: I first recorded 23-28 Sep from a secondary source. The 2026 festival actually ENDS on Sunday 27. Monday 28 is not a Merce day at all.
events.what_lluis_gets: He lands 13:15 on Saturday 26. That evening is the correfoc infantil in the afternoon and the Correfoc de la Merce after dark. Sunday 27 ends with the Piromusical at 22:00.
events.piromusical: 22:00 Sunday 27 September at BOGATELL BEACH - moved from Montjuic this year because the fairground is being renovated. Music chosen by a well-known Catalan band.
events.castellers: Thursday 24 at midday - he misses these, he is still in the air.
events.scale: 109 concerts across 14 venues and 16 stages; about 500 activities in total.
events.districts: First year it reaches all 10 districts - which is the answer to his 'not touristy' ask: the neighbourhood programme is real, not a token.
events.guest_city: Shanghai, with articulated dragons at the Forum. New stage at Placa de les Glories.

beget.access: GIV-5223 off the C-38 between Camprodon and Mollo - 14 km of continuous curves. That is the reason it stayed remote, and the reason it is a slow drive at the end of a long one.

beget.access_to_majestat: Visits confirmed through Camprodon tourism, 972 74 00 10 / turisme@camprodon.cat. It is NOT simply open - this is the whole reason to go, so it gets phoned.

montrebei.parking: Reservation is MANDATORY all year, even on free-access days, and must be made at least 24 hours ahead. La Masieta (the main car park) runs 08:30-16:45 outside high season. Vehicles over 2.30 m high cannot enter - a rental car is fine.
montrebei.alternative: La Pertusa car park is free, open 24 h, and needs no reservation.
montrebei.caution: Non-refundable, one day, one vehicle. Poor phone coverage at the site - download the confirmation before leaving.

nuria.how: Drive to Ribes de Freser (1h46), then the rack railway. The train does all the climbing, which is exactly why this one suits the group.
nuria.fares: Return: adult 14-64 EUR 33, over-65 EUR 28, child 4-13 EUR 21.50, under-4 free. The ticket includes the Coma del Clot cable car, the exhibitions and the basilica.
nuria.frequency: PATTERN, NOT A 2026 FACT: after early September the service has run nine circulations on weekdays and fourteen at weekends and on holidays through to end October. A weekday visit therefore has materially fewer trains, and the last one down governs the day.
needs: FGC's published 2026 October calendar - exact first and last train. This decides the day and must not be guessed.

empuries.proposed_date: Wed 30 September 2026 - chosen, not defaulted. The site closes at 20:00 until 30 Sep and 18:00 from 1 Oct. Sunset is 19:31 and golden hour 18:54-19:31, so the 30th is the last date in the fortnight when you can be inside the ruins while the light turns.
empuries.ap7: Toll-free between Tarragona and La Jonquera since 1 Sep 2021, still is. Side effect: it became the Barcelona commuter corridor and the metropolitan stretch jams near-daily, which is why the routed 1h42 is a floor. In Aug 2026 the Generalitat opened a working group on reinstating the tolls - nothing decided, nothing that bites before these dates.
empuries.parking: MAC-Empuries has NO car park of its own; surrounding lots are municipal or private. The municipal parking by the Hostal Empuries is normally free outside mid-Sep to July. Reserved reduced-mobility bays in front of the Visitor Reception Centre.
empuries.accessibility: Greek city adapted along most of its length; a specific signposted accessible route into the Roman city, but parts of the Roman city have steps and awkward paving. Audio guides carry a magnetic loop, as do reception and the shop.

montrebei.CORRECTION: I described this to LLuis as 'arguably the most spectacular EASY walk in Catalonia'. That was wrong for this group and he marked it IN partly on my wording. Rutes Pirineus grades the classic route MEDIUM, not easy: 9.2 km, 3h10 walking, 150 m gain.
montrebei.the_real_problem: Not the distance - the exposure. The path carved into the gorge wall is between 0.6 m and 1.5 m wide, with a drop of 40-60 m to the river. There are handrails fixed to the rock but SOME SECTIONS HAVE NONE and others are deteriorating, and there is no barrier on the void side. Rutes Pirineus says explicitly it is not recommended for anyone with vertigo or mobility limitations.

the_short_option.what: La Masieta to the mouth of the gorge and back.
the_short_option.time: About 30 minutes each way - roughly 4 km round trip, which is exactly LLuis's stated budget.
the_short_option.milestone: The Sant Jaume hanging bridge is 15 minutes in.
the_short_option.catch: You reach the gorge and look into it, then turn round before the carved path. The carved path IS the thing people come for, so this is seeing it rather than doing it. That may still be worth a 3h25 drive; it may not. LLuis's call, not mine.

montrebei.montfalco_side: Worse for this group, not better: the Montfalco walkways are 16-17 km round trip with about 1,000 m of ascent and aerial staircases. Rule it out.
montrebei.parking: Booking mandatory year-round, at least 24 h ahead, non-refundable, one day one vehicle. La Masieta 08:30-16:45 off-season. No phone signal on site - download the pass first.
montrebei.status: FLAGGED TO LLUIS - awaiting his decision on the short option versus dropping it.

calendar_shape.conclusion: The two Mondays are family days by default. The weekends carry the trips that have a weekend-only element. Empuries is one of the few things open every day, so it can absorb a midweek slot.

plan._why: Built from the constraints outwards, not from preference. The two Mondays are family days because Catalonia shuts on Mondays. Empuries is pinned to 30 Sep by its own closing time. Gosol needs a weekend for the museum. Vallbona needs Tue-Sat. Everything else fills in around those four fixed points. Family days are flexible, so they absorb the slack.

fixed_to_a_weekday.why: Closed non-holiday Mondays and the published table shows no Sunday. Visits are guided at fixed times, so arrival has to match one: 10:30, 12:30, 16:00 Catalan; 11:30, 13:30, 17:00 Spanish; 18:00 Catalan to 31 Oct.
Recent pattern is 14 circulations at weekends against 9 on weekdays. The last train down governs the day, so the thin weekday service is a real constraint.

The museum publishes summer hours to 22 Sep and winter hours from November and says nothing about October. A secondary source said weekends and holidays only; the museum's own pages do not confirm it. 973 37 29 77.

any_day.caveat: Guided town tour daily at 11:00 - leave Barcelona by 09:00. Poblet closes 17:45 until 12 Oct, which covers the whole stay. Headphones compulsory at Poblet.
Hours for the mikve and monastery still to pin down.
Can Casades information centre only opens 10:00-15:00.
Nothing to open. Sea about 22 C.
Depends on his friends, not on opening hours.
Parking must be booked at least 24 h ahead - so not spontaneous. Still awaiting his decision on whether it goes in at all.

destinations.name: La Merce - Barcelona's Festa Major
destinations.family_why: Flat, in town, and you dip in and out. But choose: the correfoc is fire and a dense crowd.
destinations.what: Barcelona's Festa Major, 23-27 September 2026. LLuis lands 13:15 on the 26th, so he gets the last two days - the Correfoc de la Merce that same evening, and the Piromusical closing the festival at 22:00 on the 27th, on Bogatell beach this year rather than Montjuic. About 500 activities, 109 concerts over 14 venues and 16 stages; 2026 is the first year it reaches all ten districts, which is the answer to wanting the neighbourhood version rather than the postcard one.
destinations.walk: City walking, flat, abandon at will.
destinations.when: SATURDAY 26 AND SUNDAY 27 SEPTEMBER ONLY. The festival ends on the 27th - there is no Merce on Monday the 28th.
gaps: The per-district programme was still pending when checked - that is the piece that actually answers 'not the touristy version'.
The castellers are Thursday 24 at midday. He is in the air. Lost.

destinations.name: Montseny - Santa Fe
destinations.family_why: Two walks and you choose on the day - one of them is pram-passable.
destinations.what: Beech and silver fir above the Valles, and the gentlest first outing on the list. Base at the Can Casades information centre: exhibition, sequoias in the garden, picnic area of three tables and a fountain. Early October is the very start of the bolets.
destinations.walk: Font del Frare: 1 km circular, about 30 minutes, purple waymarks, adapted, passable with a pram. Or the Volta al Panta de Santa Fe: 2.7 km, flat and well marked through forest, wetland and wooden walkways - but roots, loose stone and stream crossings, so the surface decides it, not the distance.
destinations.food: Hostal Santa Fe - traditional Catalan and Montseny cooking. 93 847 50 11, book at weekends.
destinations.when: Any day. Can Casades opens 10:00-15:00 only, so collect maps early. 938 475 113.

destinations.name: Empuries, Sant Marti and Cala Montgo
destinations.family_why: Flat and laid out on the sand. The Greek city is adapted along most of its length; parts of the Roman city have steps and awkward paving, and that is the half to skip.
destinations.what: A Greek harbour and a Roman city lying on the beach, a walled village of forty people with lunch on its square sixty metres from the gate, and a swim at Cala Montgo afterwards. EUR 7, EUR 5 for over-65s, under-16s free. No car park of its own, but the municipal parking is normally free at this time of year.
destinations.walk: Passeig d'Empuries: about 2.5 km one way, paved throughout, built 1992, pine-shaded, almost no elevation change, abandonable anywhere. The cami de ronda continues to Cala Montgo but that is over 5 km - held back, and Cala Montgo becomes a five-minute drive instead.
destinations.food: Meson del Conde, Placa Major 4, Sant Marti - on the square since 1965. 972 77 03 06. CLOSED MONDAYS, and on a weekday it stops at 18:00, so it is lunch not dinner.
destinations.when: Open every day, so a plain visit goes anywhere. But it closes 20:00 to 30 SEPTEMBER and 18:00 from 1 October, and sunset is 19:31 - WEDNESDAY 30 SEPTEMBER is the only day left where you can be inside the ruins in golden light. Sunday 4 October is free entry instead.

destinations.name: Segarra: Montfalco Murallat, Guimera, Vallbona
destinations.family_why: Montfalco is level once you are through the gate. GUIMERA IS THE PROBLEM - built on a steep hillside, its lanes stepped throughout. Vallbona is a flat guided visit.
destinations.what: Dry, empty, upland Catalonia - the part of the country that never got rich and so never got rebuilt. Montfalco Murallat is a 13th-century walled village of fifteen houses with one gate, one circular street, the old cistern and the communal bread oven, still lived in.
destinations.walk: Barely a walk. A lap of a village you could cross in ninety seconds, plus a path round the outside of the walls.
destinations.food: Cister de Vallbona in Vallbona de les Monges - homemade, local produce. Also Sant Jordi in Guimera and Restaurant Montfalco in Les Oluges.
destinations.when: TUESDAY TO SATURDAY. Vallbona closes non-holiday Mondays and publishes no Sunday hours, and the visit is GUIDED AT FIXED TIMES: 10:30, 12:30, 16:00 Catalan; 11:30, 13:30, 17:00 Spanish; plus 18:00 Catalan to 31 October. March-October 10:30-13:30 and 16:30-18:30. 973 330 266.
gaps: None of the three restaurants publishes hours anywhere reachable.
Montfalco's car park is free, 15-20 cars - but the climb is an 800 m lane wide enough for one vehicle.

destinations.name: Gosol and the Cadi
destinations.family_why: The square and the Gresolet viewpoint are fine. The old village ruins are short but rough and uphill - that is the bit to leave out.
destinations.what: Under the Pedraforca, in the village where Picasso spent the summer of 1906 and left with the beginnings of Cubism. The Centre Picasso holds the most representative collection of the 302 works from that period. EUR 6 / 5 / 3.
destinations.walk: Gresolet viewpoint, about 30 minutes, easy, for the north face of the Pedraforca head on. Also a 2 km circular family route.
destinations.food: Not sourced. Every source found recommends a picnic, which is a real answer in a village this size but wants checking against October weather.
destinations.when: PROBABLY WEEKENDS - but nobody will say. The museum publishes summer hours (20 June-22 September) and winter hours (November-March) and is silent on October, which is exactly when he would go. 973 37 29 77, they answer on WhatsApp.
gaps: October opening hours genuinely unpublished. An earlier 'weekends and holidays only' answer came from a secondary source and the museum's own pages do not confirm it.
No restaurant sourced in Gosol or Saldes.

destinations.name: Besalu
destinations.family_why: Street level and small. THE 36 STEPS DOWN INTO THE MIKVE are the only obstacle, and easy to sit out on the square.
destinations.what: The one he has seen but would go back to. The 11th-century bridge is the postcard; the mikve - the Jewish ritual bath beside the old synagogue - is what most people miss, a subterranean Romanesque chamber reached by 36 steps down to the pool that took river water. Sant Pere was founded in 977.
destinations.walk: Street level. The Anella Verda runs out through the market gardens if you want more.
destinations.food: Pont Vell, beside the Romanesque bridge - Michelin-listed, family-run, local produce, and the view is the point. Can Quei in the old centre for plainer traditional cooking; also Curia Reial and El Jardi de Can Marc for rice and grilled meats.
destinations.when: Any day - nothing here is time-critical.
gaps: Opening hours for the mikve and the monastery not yet pinned to October.

destinations.name: Vall de Nuria
destinations.family_why: THE MOST ACCESSIBLE GOOD DAY ON THE LIST. The train does all the climbing; the lake path has been improved for accessibility and there is a lift specifically to reach the cable car.
destinations.what: Drive to Ribes de Freser and hand the mountain to a rack railway that has been climbing it since 1931. The valley at the top has no road into it at all, which is why it feels the way it does. 1,964 m, in October, with the larches going. Return fares EUR 33 adult, EUR 28 over-65, EUR 21.50 child 4-13, under-4s free - including the Coma del Clot cable car, the exhibitions and the basilica.
destinations.walk: The Volta al Llac: flat, easy, free, under half an hour. Small wooden bridges, streams and fountains, and the 17th-century hermitage of Sant Gil.
destinations.food: The sanctuary complex has its own places. Not researched - a captive site, which usually means adequate rather than good.
destinations.when: A WEEKEND IS MATERIALLY BETTER. Recent pattern is fourteen circulations at weekends against nine on weekdays from early September to end October, and the last train down governs the day.
gaps: FGC's actual 2026 October timetable could not be sourced, and it is the single thing that decides this day. Check it before fixing a date.

destinations.name: L'Ametlla de Mar - Cala Forn
destinations.family_why: Access is an asphalt path with a car park at the end of it. Nobody has to scramble down anything - which is why this is the beach day rather than a prettier cove further north.
destinations.what: The Costa Daurada nobody photographs. Cala Forn is a small U-shaped cove held between rocks, between the Sant Jordi d'Alfama and Tres Cales developments. Sea about 22 C - the last realistic swimming day of the trip.
destinations.walk: From the cove the GR-92 runs south towards L'Ampolla with wooden walkways dropping into one cove after another. Walk as much or as little as you want and turn back.
destinations.food: La Llotja on the port - chef Marc Miro, in the Michelin guide, and the rice is what everyone cites. BUT it runs EUR 60-100 a head, which is above the local register asked for. Either the one blowout, or find a port-front alternative.
destinations.when: Any day. Nothing opens or shuts.
gaps: No modest port-front alternative to La Llotja researched yet.

destinations.name: Girona - friends
destinations.family_why: Walking is incidental. The cathedral staircase and the wall circuit are the only climbs and both are optional.
destinations.what: Not a sightseeing day. He is seeing friends, so this is a social day that happens to be in a beautiful place, and it has deliberately not been programmed.
destinations.food: Left to his friends, who will know better.
destinations.when: Any day - depends on his friends, not on opening hours.

destinations.name: Montblanc and Poblet
destinations.family_why: The town is walkable and mostly level; the pas de ronda along the top of the ramparts is the optional hard part. Poblet's interior is largely flat.
destinations.what: The best-preserved town walls in Catalonia - about 1,500 m of 14th-century curtain with 30 towers - and half an hour further on, the royal pantheon of the Crown of Aragon.
destinations.walk: The pas de ronda round the top of the walls, if wanted. Otherwise level streets.
destinations.food: Not sourced. The Conca de Barbera is good wine country and the tourist office keeps a list.
destinations.when: Any day, but there is a GUIDED TOWN TOUR EVERY DAY AT 11:00, two hours, from the tourist office - Santa Maria, Sant Miquel, the old hospital of Santa Magdalena, the walls and the Sant Jordi gate. Leave Barcelona by 09:00. Poblet closes 17:45 until 12 October, which covers the whole stay; EUR 10.50, self-guided by app and HEADPHONES ARE COMPULSORY. Office 977 861 733, Mon-Fri 9-15, Sat 10-14 and 16-18.
gaps: Montblanc walls and museum opening hours not published anywhere reachable.

destinations.name: Sitges - a film and dinner
destinations.family_why: Flat seafront town. Busy during the festival - that is the only caution.
destinations.what: The 59th Sitges festival runs 8-18 October. Announced so far: a strand of Spanish genre productions, a retrospective of fantastic classics, an Asian fantastic strand, and a 50th-anniversary tribute to CARRIE - which is the most concrete thing to build an evening around. Last year the main house was the Auditori at the Hotel Melia, 1,380 seats, with the Tramuntana room, Cinema Casino Prado, l'Escorxador, the Miramar centre and the Mercat Vell for the family programme.
destinations.walk: Seafront and old town, flat throughout.
destinations.food: To be chosen with the film, once there is a film.
destinations.when: THURSDAY 8, FRIDAY 9 OR SATURDAY 10 OCTOBER. The festival runs to the 18th but he flies on the 11th. Saturday is the busiest; Friday is probably the civilised one.
gaps: Screening times and the ticket on-sale date are not published, so the film cannot be chosen yet. This is the outstanding ask.

destinations.name: Congost de Mont-rebei
destinations.family_why: NOT FOR THE GROUP. Graded medium, not easy: 9.2 km, 3h10, with a path 0.6-1.5 m wide above a 40-60 m drop, handrails missing in places and no barrier over the void. Explicitly not recommended for vertigo or limited mobility.
destinations.what: A walkway cut into a vertical limestone gorge above turquoise water, and the furthest thing on the list. Still awaiting a decision on whether it goes in at all.
destinations.walk: The short option is La Masieta to the mouth of the gorge and back - about 30 minutes each way, roughly 4 km, exactly the stated budget. But you turn round before the carved path, which is the reason people come. Seeing it rather than doing it.
destinations.when: Any day, but PARKING MUST BE BOOKED AT LEAST 24 HOURS AHEAD, all year, non-refundable, one day one vehicle. La Masieta runs 08:30-16:45 off-season and there is no phone signal on site, so download the pass first.
gaps: Awaiting LLuis's decision: short version, drop it, or he walks it alone.
Whether the exposure begins before the gorge mouth or only inside it.

shots.title: The piromusical off Bogatell
shots.subject: La Merce's closing fireworks, 22:00 Sunday 27 September. Moved to the beach this year from Montjuic, which means for the first time they go up over water.
shots.vantage: The beach itself, north of the crowd, far enough back to get the reflection in the wet sand. Arrive early - this is the single biggest gathering of the fortnight.
shots.light: Full dark. Moon 99% and rising, so the sky will not be black - expect a bright, milky background rather than a clean one.
shots.craft: Tripod, ISO 100, f/11, 2-4 second exposures on bulb. The mistake is zooming in: leave the skyline in or it is just sparks.

shots.title: The Greek mole at Empuries, 19:00
shots.subject: The harbour wall running into the water on the seaward edge of the Greek city - the reason the city is where it is.
shots.vantage: Low, on the sand at the site's edge, shooting west-north-west.
shots.light: 30 September, sunset 19:31 at azimuth 267. Golden hour 18:54-19:31, and the site does not close until 20:00 - the only day in the fortnight both are true.
shots.craft: Wide, 20-24 mm, f/8, and get the camera down near the stone so the wet surface catches it.

shots.title: Montfalco Murallat from outside the wall
shots.subject: Fifteen houses, one gate, one circular street, and a 13th-century wall still holding it all in. From outside it reads as a single building.
shots.vantage: The path that runs right round the outside of the walls. Walk to the far side so the village is between you and the light.
shots.light: 2 October, sunset 19:35. Late afternoon - the stone is the whole subject and it needs raking light, not overhead.
shots.craft: 85-135 mm to compress the wall into a single mass. Wide makes it look small, which is the opposite of the point.

shots.title: The Pedraforca from Gresolet
shots.subject: The north face head on - the mountain that made Gosol worth Picasso's summer.
shots.vantage: The Gresolet viewpoint, about 30 minutes' easy walk. The one place the north face is not foreshortened.
shots.light: 3 October, sunset 19:32, moon at 51%. A north face is in shadow most of the day; early morning or the last hour is when it has any modelling at all.
shots.craft: 50-85 mm. Include some of the beech in the foreground or the scale disappears.

shots.title: Sant Gil and the lake, Nuria
shots.subject: The 17th-century hermitage on the Volta al Llac, with the cirque behind it.
shots.vantage: The far side of the lake on the flat circuit - about fifteen minutes round, and the reflection is the shot.
shots.light: 6 October, sunset 19:25 but the valley walls take the sun long before that. Moon only 19% - a genuinely dark sky if you stay, though the last train governs that.
shots.craft: 35-50 mm, f/8. Wind kills the reflection, so shoot it early if the water is still.
